title: Miller Back from Paternity List for Game 4; Latest Updates on Morejon’s Status】
body:
SAN DIEGO – The Padres are poised to reinforce their bullpen on Wednesday night as left‑hander Mason Miller returns from the paternity list, and they may also have rookie right‑hander Adrian Morejon ready to pitch in Game 4 of the National League Division Series at Petco Park. The moves come as San Diego looks to stave off a surging opponent and force a decisive Game 5 in the best‑of‑five series.

Miller, who was placed on the paternity list earlier this week, is expected to be cleared for duty after a brief stint away from the club. The 28‑year‑old reliever has been a steady presence out of the pen all season, posting a 3.12 ERA over 71 innings with a strikeout‑to‑walk ratio of 4.1. His left‑handed delivery gives the Padres a valuable matchup tool against right‑handed power hitters who have been instrumental in the series thus far. Manager Mike Shildt indicated that Miller will be available “to eat innings and provide a left‑handed option in the later frames,” underscoring the importance of bullpen depth in a tightly contested series.

The potential activation of Adrian Morejon adds another layer of intrigue. The 22‑year‑old right‑hander, who made his major‑league debut earlier this season, has been working out of the Padres’ Triple‑A affiliate, where he has compiled a 2.68 ERA with 78 strikeouts in 66 innings. Morejon’s fastball sits in the mid‑90s and is complemented by a sharp breaking ball that has been effective against both left‑ and right‑handed batters. While he has not yet appeared in the postseason, Shildt hinted that the rookie could be called upon if the bullpen needs an extra arm, especially if the series extends to a fifth game.

The timing of Miller’s return could not be more critical. In Game 3, the Padres’ bullpen was stretched thin, surrendering a three‑run lead in the eighth inning that ultimately cost them the win. The loss placed San Diego down 2‑1 in the series, and the margin for error has narrowed dramatically. By reinstating Miller, the Padres not only restore a proven left‑handed specialist but also gain flexibility to shuffle relievers and preserve their closer for a potential high‑leverage situation. Analysts note that the left‑right matchup dynamics will be a focal point, as the opposition’s lineup features several left‑handed sluggers who thrive against same‑handed pitching.

Beyond the immediate tactical considerations, Miller’s return carries an emotional undertone. He spent the past week in the company of his newborn son, a milestone that resonated with teammates and fans alike. Shildt praised Miller’s “professionalism and dedication,” noting that his presence in the clubhouse adds a morale boost that extends beyond the mound. The Padres, who have cultivated a reputation for strong team chemistry, will likely draw on that camaraderie as they confront a resilient opponent seeking to close out the series.

Looking ahead, the Padres must execute a balanced game plan that leverages Miller’s left‑handed proficiency while remaining open to deploying Morejon if the situation demands. The upcoming Game 4 will serve as a litmus test for the team’s ability to adapt under pressure and could set the tone for a decisive Game 5 if the series extends. With the bullpen bolstered and the roster approaching full strength, San Diego appears ready to challenge the momentum of its adversary and keep its postseason hopes alive.
